newsitem.title: FRANCE: French ex-minister in court for perjury.
newsitem.headline: French ex-minister in court for perjury.

text.p: A state prosecutor on Thursday requested a 15-month suspended jail sentence for French ex-cabinet minister Jacques Mellick for lying in court to try to shield ex-tycoon Bernard Tapie in a soccer scandal.

The hearing, in the northern town of Valenciennes, was the conclusion of a thriller case which captivated France and has already landed Tapie in prison for rigging a game between his ex-European champions Marseille and Valenciennes.

Mellick had testified that he was in Tapie's Paris office on June 17, 1993, and saw no trace of a soccer coach who had testified earlier that he was there at that time, being bribed by Tapie to take responsibility for the match-rigging.

Mellick's lie was exposed by a picture taken at a ceremony he attended on that day in Valenciennes, where he served as mayor, and by records of motorway toll payments showing he could not have arrived in time for the purported meeting with Tapie.
Mellick confessed during the match-rigging trial that he was lying.
He told the court on Thursday that be had been under pressure from Tapie and agreed to help him so that the tycoon would not close down a factory he had in Valenciennes.
"I believed it was not serious as it was not a case of murder or rape. I did not know how to get out of it," he said.

Mellick was convicted last year of also trying to get his assistant to lie in court to confirm his meeting with Tapie. He was given a two-month suspended sentence on a charge of interfering with a witness and banned for two years from running for public office.
He has resigned his seat in parliament and did not run for re-election as Valenciennes mayor.
Tapie, also a former cabinet minister, is serving an eight-month jail term over the rigged match.
The Valenciennes court is to announce its verdict in the Mellick case on March 6.
